title: Squared Fourier coefficients under random restrictions
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $\delta\in\mathbb R$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The expected square of the ambient restriction Fourier coefficient at $S$, when each coordinate is independently included in the free set with weight parameter $\delta$, equals $\displaystyle\sum_{U\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\mathbf 1_{S\subseteq U}\,\delta^{|S|}(1-\delta)^{|U\setminus S|}\,\widehat f(U)^2$, where $\widehat f(U)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$S$ is a subset of the coordinates
